statement.p: Let f(x,y)=x^2e^{x^2} and let R be the triangle bounded by the lines x=4, x=y/2, and y=x in the xy-plane.

(a) Express \int_R{f}\,dA as a double integral in two different ways by filling in the values for the integrals below. (For one of these it will be necessary to write the double integral as a sum of two integrals, as indicated; for the other, it can be written as a single integral.)
where a = , b = , c = , and d = .
And \int_R{f}\,dA = \int_a^b\int_c^d f(x,y)\, d d + \int_m^n\int_p^q f(x,y)\, d d
where a = , b = , c = , d = , m = , n = , p = , and q = .
(b) Evaluate one of your integrals to find the value of \int_R{f}\,dA.

static.solution:
(a) The line x=y/2 is the line y=2 x, and y=x and y=2 x intersect at x=0. Thus, R is the shaded region in the figure below.
One expression for the integral is \int_R f\,dA =\int_0^{4}\int_x^{2 x} x^2e^{x^2}\,dy\,dx. Another expression is obtained by reversing the order of integration. When we do this, it is necessary to split R into two regions on a line parallel to the x-axis along the point of intersection of y=x and x=4; this line is y=4. Then we obtain \int_Rf\,dA = \int_0^{4}\int_{y/2}^{y} x^2e^{x^2}\,dx\,dy+ \int_{4}^{8} \int_{y/2}^{4} x^2e^{x^2}\,dx\,dy.
(b) We evaluate the first integral. Integrating with respect to y first: \int_0^{4}\int_x^{2 x} x^2 e^{x^2}\,dy\,dx = \int_0^{4} (x^2e^{x^2}y)\bigg|_x^{2 x}\,dx = \int_0^{4} x^3 e^{x^2}\,dx. To do the second integral, we use integration by parts with u=x^2, v'=xe^{x^2}. Then u'=2x and v=\frac{1}{2}e^{x^2}, so \int_0^{4} x^3e^{x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} x^2e^{x^2}\bigg|_0^{4} - \int_0^{4} x e^{x^2}\,dx. The second integral is then easily obtained, giving \int_0^{4} x^3e^{x^2}\,dx = \left(\frac{1}{2} x^2e^{x^2} - \frac{1}{2} e^{x^2}\right)\bigg|_0^{4} = 8 e^{16} - \frac{1}{2} e^{16} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{15}{2} e^{16} + \frac12.
